sources.title: Does routine compression undo LLM unlearning? A short
sources.snippet: The scope of this project was narrow: only 1 model (Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct), 1 TOFU split (forget10), and 3 unlearning methods. There are no doubt many limitations that I'm not aware of too. Super open to any and all feedback! Takeaways The main technical takeaway is that standard compression isn't a practical attack here.

sources.snippet: TOFU validation TOFU is an LLM unlearning benchmark: a model is finetuned to memorize synthetic author biographies, then asked to forget a subset ("forget10" = 10%) while preserving the rest ("retain").

sources.title: TOFU Dataset Files | sail-sg/closer-look-LLM-unlearning | DeepWiki
sources.snippet: This page describes all data files under data/tofu/. It covers the file inventory, record schemas, split naming conventions, and the fictitious author domain used by the TOFU benchmark. For how these files are loaded and used during training, see the Dataset Module (4.1). For how they are used in the Fictitious Unlearning experimental scenario, see 3.1. For the real-world dataset files, see 6.2.

sources.snippet: For each architecture, we have finetuned with four different splits of the TOFU datasets: full, retain90, retain95, retain99, for a total of 16 finetuned models. The first serves as the target (base model for unlearning) and the rest are retain models used to measure performance against for each forget split.
